top_signals.title: Rwanda Wins F1 Hosting Rights in Bet on Tourism
top_signals.summary: Rwanda has been chosen to host Formula 1’s return to Africa, beating competition from South Africa and Morocco. With the first Grand Prix planned for the early 2030s, the country is betting on a new circuit, airport and hotels to drive tourism, create jobs and boost its economy. But can the benefits justify the cost? On Bloomberg’s Next Africa, Jennifer Zabasajja speaks to Rwanda’s Sports Minister Nelly Mukazayire about funding, jobs and the country’s sporting ambitions. Sports economist Victor Matheson examines the potential returns and how much revenue could stay in Rwanda, while FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem discusses the winning bid, affordability and the possibility of more African races. Bloomberg’s Loni Prinsloo looks at the reaction across the continent, South Africa’s disappointment and the infrastructure challenges ahead. (Source: Bloomberg)
